title: Practice Passage 8: Why Green Roofs Matter in Modern Cities

passage.title: Why Green Roofs Matter in Modern Cities
passage.sub_title: How living rooftops are combating the urban heat island effect, fostering biodiversity, and managing storm runoff.
passage.content_html:
Paragraph A

[A1] As cities continue to expand, many natural areas disappear beneath roads, buildings, and parking spaces. [A2] This rapid development changes the local environment in several ways, including higher temperatures and reduced habitats for wildlife. [A3] To address some of these problems, architects and environmental scientists have become increasingly interested in green roofs. [A4] A green roof is a building roof that is partially or completely covered with living plants grown in a specially designed layer of soil.

Paragraph B

[B1] Although green roofs may appear to be a modern invention, the basic idea has existed for centuries. [B2] Historical records show that people in several cold regions placed grass and soil on rooftops to improve insulation. [B3] Modern green roofs, however, use carefully engineered drainage systems and lightweight materials that make them suitable for many different types of buildings. [B4] Advances in construction technology have made these systems easier to install than they were several decades ago.

Paragraph C

[C1] One of the most noticeable advantages of green roofs is their ability to reduce building temperatures during warm weather. [C2] Plants absorb sunlight that would otherwise heat traditional roofing materials. [C3] As a result, some buildings require less electricity for air conditioning during summer months. [C4] Researchers have reported energy savings in many cities, although the amount varies according to climate, roof size, and plant type.

Paragraph D

[D1] Green roofs also improve urban biodiversity. [D2] Birds, bees, butterflies, and other insects often use rooftop vegetation as resting or feeding areas. [D3] In cities where parks are limited, these roofs can provide small but valuable habitats. [D4] Scientists caution, however, that a single green roof cannot replace large natural ecosystems.

Paragraph E

[E1] Another important benefit is improved rainwater management. [E2] During storms, plants and soil temporarily retain part of the rainfall. [E3] This slows the movement of water into drains, reducing pressure on urban drainage systems. [E4] Nevertheless, green roofs are only one component of effective flood management and cannot prevent flooding in every situation.

Paragraph F

[F1] Despite these benefits, green roofs are not suitable for every building. [F2] Older buildings may require structural improvements before additional weight can be safely supported. [F3] Installation costs are generally higher than those of conventional roofs. [F4] However, supporters argue that lower energy use and reduced maintenance costs can offset some of the initial expense over time.

Paragraph G

[G1] Interest in green roofs continues to increase around the world. [G2] Some city governments encourage their construction through financial incentives or planning policies. [G3] Others prefer to educate building owners about their environmental benefits rather than introduce new regulations. [G4] Experts agree that green roofs should be considered as part of a broader strategy for creating more sustainable cities.

questions.instruction_text: Do the following statements agree with the information given in the reading passage? Write TRUE, FALSE, or NOT GIVEN.

question_data.text: Green roofs were first developed within the last fifty years.
question_data.common_mistake: Believing modern green roofs represent the origin of the technology.
